final_message:
Fixed the bug and wrote `answer.json`; `answer.json` is gitignored, which is why it doesn't show in `git status`.

**Root cause:** `mrr()` in `billing/reports.py` filtered subscriptions with `subscription["customer_id"] not in ("active", "past_due")`. It checked the customer ID against status names, so every subscription was skipped and the result was `{}`. It now checks `subscription["status"]`.

**Verification:** I ran your reproduction test as a temporary file in `tests/` and removed it afterward. It passes, and the full suite passes (25 tests).

**`answer.json`:** `{"file": "reports.py", "function": "mrr"}`

steps.command: cd billing && ls && cat reports.py && cat ../tests/conftest.py

cd .. && sed -i 's/if subscription\["customer_id"\] not in/if subscription["status"] not in/' billing/reports.py && cat > /tmp/t.py <<'E'
from billing import reports
def test_mrr_and_aging(world):
    from billing import catalog
    yearly = catalog.create_price(world.ctx, world.plan["id"], "usd", "flat", unit_amount=12000, interval="year")
    a = world.customer()
    b = world.customer(email="b@example.com", card=False)
    world.engine.subscribe(a["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 3)])
    world.engine.subscribe(b["id"], [(yearly["id"], 1)])
    assert reports.mrr(world.ctx) == {"usd": 3000 + 1000}
    world.clock.advance_days(40)
    aging = reports.aging(world.ctx, world.clock.now())
    assert aging["usd"]["31-60"] == 12000
E
cp /tmp/t.py tests/test_tmp.py && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -15; rm tests/test_tmp.py

cd .. && cat > tests/test_tmp.py <<'E'

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -15; rm tests/test_tmp.py
pwd; ls answer.json; git check-ignore -v answer.json
